lesson.subject: numeracy
lesson.title: Angles on a Line and at a Point
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 1, Session 3
lesson.fileName: Session 3 - Angles on a Line and at a Point.pptx

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Measurement, Year 6 (VC2M6M04): angles on a straight line and at a point; use them to find unknown angles, communicating reasoning
plan.shape: example-first for the two angle facts, then a practice round mixing them, because choosing the right whole is the new decision
plan.criticalFeature: find the whole first (90°, 180° or 360°), then subtract what you know
decisionPoints: the choice check on the straight line
plan.anchor: quarter turn 90°, half turn 180°, full turn 360°
plan.catchUp: Missed Sessions 1 or 2? Show the anchor: a straight line is a half turn, 180°, a full turn 360°; that is all today needs.

manipulatives: A protractor for every student, to check answers
Paper strips or rulers to show a straight line
studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The anchor on the board: quarter turn 90°, half turn 180°, full turn 360°

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Straight lines, points, right angles, worded problems and thinking questions.
resources.title: Angles on a Line and at a Point
resources.subtitle: Find the whole first, then subtract.

items.prompt: Find a.
Find b.
Find c.
Find d.
Find e.
Find f.
Find g.
Find h.
Find p.
Find q.
Two complementary angles are equal. How big is each one?
Two supplementary angles are equal. How big is each one?

example.prompt: A ladder leans on a wall and makes 65° with the ground. What angle does it make with the ground on the other side of its foot?
steps: The ground is a straight line: 180°.

items.prompt: At the bottom of a skate ramp, the ramp makes 28° with the ground. What is the other angle on the straight line?
A pizza is cut into 3 slices from the centre. Two slices have angles of 110° and 130°. What is the angle of the third slice?
A coach draws two lines that meet at a right angle. A player runs along a line 35° from one of them, inside the right angle. What angle is left?
A Ferris wheel has 8 equal spokes. What is the angle between two spokes next to each other?

example.prompt: Can a straight line hold two angles of 100°? Explain.

items.prompt: One angle on a straight line is 140°. Ali says the other is 220° because 360 - 140 = 220. Explain his mistake and find the right answer.
Can two obtuse angles sit next to each other on a straight line? Explain.
items.answer: No. Two angles over 90° add to more than 180°.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Angle puzzles with number sentences, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Angle Puzzles
resources.subtitle: Write a number sentence, then solve it.

sections.title: Equal angles
sections.intro: When angles are marked with the same letter, they are the same size. Write a number sentence and share the whole equally.

example.prompt: Three angles marked x sit on a straight line. Find x.

items.prompt: Two angles marked a and a 40° angle sit on a straight line. Find a.
Four equal angles meet at a point. How big is each?
Five angles marked b meet at a point. Find b.

example.prompt: Two angles on a straight line: one is double the other. Find both.
steps: Call the small one s. The big one is 2 x s.
s = 60°, so the angles are 60° and 120°.

items.prompt: Two complementary angles: one is double the other. Find both.
Three angles at a point: the second is double the first, and the third is triple the first. Find all three.

example.prompt: Make a straight-line puzzle with a missing angle of 35°.
steps: The missing angle and the known angle make 180°.
Puzzle: a straight line with 145° and x.

items.prompt: Make a puzzle around a point where the missing angle is 100°. Draw it and write the answer.
items.answer: any angles adding to 260° with a missing 100°

items.prompt: Make a right-angle puzzle where the missing angle is 18°. Draw it and write the answer.
items.answer: a right angle split into 72° and 18°

resources.description: For students who need more guidance: the whole is given, number sentences are started.
resources.title: Missing Angles: Step by Step

sections.title: Around a point: the whole is 360°

slides.notes: Open Session 3 of the angles week. One line: today we find missing angles without measuring.
Prep slide. Boards and markers, a protractor each to check answers. Print the Worksheet for all, and some Extension and Supported Worksheet copies.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with fractions, decimals and percentages again.
ASK: Which is bigger: three fifths or 0.62?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 0.62
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, move on.
Less -> turn 3/5 into tenths, then hundredths, together, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Three fifths is 0.60, so 0.62 is bigger. Tick or fix.
trap: choosing 3/5 because 5 is bigger than 2.
Fix: write both as hundredths, student compares.
notes.prep: Daily Review from Term 3 Week 9. Whole block under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Percentage to fraction
prompts: Write 45% as a fraction in its simplest form.

beats: ASK: Write 45 percent as a fraction in its simplest form.
25 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 9/20
SCAN boards for 9/20.
80%+ -> reveal, move on.
Less -> write 45/100 together, divide top and bottom by 5, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 45 hundredths simplifies to nine twentieths. Tick or fix.
trap: stopping at 45/100.
Fix: find a number that divides both, student simplifies.

beats: ASK: What is 20 percent of 250?
20 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 50
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then Fluency.
Less -> find 10% first, 25, then double it, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 10 percent is 25, so 20 percent is 50. Tick or fix.
trap: writing 20 or 230.
Fix: find 10% first, student doubles.
notes.prep: Term 3 Week 9 retrieval: percentage of an amount.

slides.title: Add with the written method: 3 digits

beats: SAY: Now the written method. Line up the places and start with the ones.
ASK: Solve it with the written method.
30 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 1 245
SCAN boards for the regrouped digits.
80%+ -> reveal, next one.
Less -> model the ones and the regroup together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 1 245. Tick or fix, and check every regroup.
trap: forgetting to add a regrouped ten.
Fix: circle each carried digit, student re-adds that column.
notes.prep: Algorithm fluency: 3 digits, then 4, then 5. Whole block under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Add with the written method: 4 digits

beats: SAY: Now 4 digits. Same method, one more column.
ASK: Solve it with the written method.
45 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 10 343
SCAN boards for the regrouped digits.
80%+ -> reveal, next one.
Less -> model the ones and the regroup together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 10 343. Tick or fix, and check every regroup.
trap: forgetting to add a regrouped ten.
Fix: circle each carried digit, student re-adds that column.

slides.title: Add with the written method: 5 digits

beats: SAY: Now 5 digits. Same method, one more column.
ASK: Solve it with the written method.
60 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 88 223
SCAN boards for the regrouped digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> model the ones and the regroup together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 88 223. Tick or fix, and check every regroup.
trap: forgetting to add a regrouped ten.
Fix: circle each carried digit, student re-adds that column.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to find unknown angles on a straight line and around a point.
successCriteria: I can say what angles on a straight line and around a point add to.
I can find an unknown angle by subtracting from 90°, 180° or 360°.
I can explain my answer using an angle fact.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Today we find angles without measuring them. We use facts instead.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: Knowing the two facts is where we start.
Finding the missing angle is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 the facts; SC2 finding the unknown is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 explaining with the fact is the stretch.

slides.title: A straight line is a half turn
slides.prompt: How many degrees in a straight line? All the way round?

beats: POINT to the straight line.
SAY: A straight line is a half turn, from our anchor.
ASK: How many degrees in a straight line? All the way round?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 180 and 360
SCAN boards for 180 and 360.
80%+ -> move on.
Less -> turn together: half turn, full turn, re-ask.
trap: writing 100 for a straight line.
Fix: add two quarter turns, student rewrites.
notes.prep: Launch after the LI: the anchor becomes today's two facts. Under 3 minutes.

slides.meaning: Two angles that add to 180°, like the two parts of a straight line.

notes.answer: two angles that add to 180 degrees
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Supplementary. Say it with me. Sup-ple-men-ta-ry.
SAY: Two angles are supplementary when they add to 180.
They fit together into a straight line.
ASK: Are 110° and 70° supplementary?
10 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, they add to 180
trap: mixing up supplementary with 90.
Fix: point to the straight line, student re-says 180.
notes.prep: Complementary (90) is taught inside the I Do; one word card keeps the load down.

slides.title: Angles on a straight line
steps: The angles on it add to 180°.

beats: POINT to the straight line.
SAY: These two angles sit on a straight line, so together they make 180.
MODEL the number sentence.
SAY: I know 120, so the missing part is 180 take away 120.
ASK: What is x?
10 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 60
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 60 degrees. And 120 plus 60 makes 180, so it checks.
trap: subtracting from 360.
Fix: trace the straight line, student uses 180.
notes.stretch: Could x be bigger than 120? What would the diagram look like?
notes.prep: The whole first, then subtract: the critical feature. SC2.

beats: POINT around the point.
SAY: These three angles go all the way round, so together they make 360.
MODEL adding what I know.
SAY: 100 and 120 make 220. The missing angle is 360 take away 220.
ASK: What is y?
15 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 140
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 140 degrees. 100, 120 and 140 make 360.
trap: subtracting from 180.
Fix: trace all the way round, student uses 360.
notes.stretch: Split y into two angles so that one is double the other.
notes.help: Add the known angles first, then count on to 360.

beats: POINT to the square corner.
SAY: The little square tells me this whole corner is 90.
MODEL the subtraction.
SAY: Angles that add to 90 are complementary. 90 take away 35.
ASK: What is z?
10 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 55
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 55 degrees. 35 plus 55 makes 90.
trap: using 180 because it is an angle.
Fix: point to the square, student uses 90.
notes.stretch: Which pairs of whole numbers are complementary and both multiples of 15?
notes.prep: Third whole: 90. Complementary named in speech; the key word card covers supplementary. SC2.

slides.title: On a straight line
slides.prompt: One angle on a straight line is 70°. What is the other?

options.misconception: subtracts from 90° (confuses the straight line with a right angle)
subtracts from 360° (uses a full turn for a straight line)

beats: SAY: Find the whole first. Then choose.
ASK: One angle on a straight line is 70. What is the other?
10 sec. Cue: voices off. Point... now.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one child: why not A?
Less -> trace a straight line and say half turn, 180, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. 180 take away 70 is 110.
trap: pointing to A or C.
Fix: ask which whole a straight line makes, student redoes.
notes.prep: First decision point: the wrong answers tell you which whole was used.

slides.title: Find the missing angle
slides.ask: Find the missing angle. Which whole did you use?
slides.pivot: say the whole out loud first: 90, 180 or 360
slides.followUp: cold call one board: which whole, and why?

items.say: 120 degrees. Three equal angles around a point, 360 shared by 3. Tick or fix.

say: Let's practise. Say the whole to yourself first,
then write the missing angle on your board.
trap: using the wrong whole.
Fix: name the shape, straight, corner or point, then redo.
notes.stretch: Write the number sentence you used for each one.
notes.help: Keep the anchor on your desk: 90, 180, 360.
notes.prep: Guided practice mixing all three wholes, so choosing the whole is the practice. SC2.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you. Find the whole first.
ASK: What is f?
20 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 132
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> lay a ruler on the straight line, say half turn 180, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 132 degrees. 48 plus 132 makes 180. Tick or fix.
trap: writing 42.
Fix: ask what the whole line makes, student uses 180.
notes.prep: The hinge before independence. Students writing 42 or 312 start with the teacher on the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Find the missing angles on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: When you finish, the early finisher option is the Extension.
Say the steps with me. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Ask: which whole did you use?
TIME 20 minutes. Check-in at question 10.
trap: mixing up 180 and 360.
Fix: name the shape first, student redoes.
notes.stretch: Extension: angle puzzles with number sentences.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: number sentences started for you.
notes.prep: Independent practice across the three wholes, worded problems and reasoning. Sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Find g. Write the number sentence.

beats: SAY: Last one. The answer and the number sentence on your board.
ASK: Find g.
30 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 145
RECORD who uses 180: they write 35 or less.
They start tomorrow's check with the teacher.
trap: forgetting the right angle.
Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 with a hidden 90: the square marker has to be read.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner how you choose the whole.

notes.answer: open - listen for straight 180, point 360, corner 90
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can find a missing angle?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with a wrong whole matters most.
ASK: Tell your partner how you choose the whole.
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: straight line 180, point 360, square corner 90
notes.prep: Self-assessment read beside the exit evidence. SC2.
